questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most important thing for me was to go to a place where I could practice my oral skills in German. Furthermore I had already lived a year in Munich and wanted to live somewhere else than in South Germany.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I got most of the information I needed from the Erasmus-coordinator at Hamborg University and then I searched a lot on the university's homepage. But sometimes it was a bit difficult to find all the relevant information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got mails from the Erasmus-coordinator.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found a room in a collective ("WG") through the website
WG-gesucht.de
. It was a bit difficult - I wrote a lot of applications to people and had some Skype-interviews, but I really think it was worth it and I can highly recommend the website WG-gesucht - it's very easy to use and probably the place in Germany where you can find most available housings.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I really liked living off campus, in the center of the city. I can recommend to check where your courses are going to take place so you don't live too far away from that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process is completely different from the way we do it in Denmark and that makes it a bit confusing and difficult but I think the university was very good at helping with information.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Some weeks before the semester started I got access to a website where I could see all the courses. Then I had to write an email to each professor and ask if it was possible to join their class and then later on I would get officially registred for the class in an online system.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could contact the Erasmus-office (but they were often very busy) and then I had a 'buddy' who already studied at the university, but she was new in Hamborg, so she didn't really know that much about it either.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, I got almost all of the courses I wanted - there were only a few I didn't get because there was overlap in the schedules. But overall it was very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In Hamborg you had the possibility of trying out different classes for the first week of the semester, and I would highly recommend you to just try out a loot of different classes if you also have that possibility. Also I will recommend that you talk with your professors about exams and ECTS-points pretty early (as soon as you know which courses you are taking) because you need to be sure that you can get the right amount of ECTS-points and that often depends on which type of exam you need to do. So just talk with your professors right away.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was very appropriate - I got challenged and learned a lot but without feeling totally overwhelmed. I had a good combination of seminars which were quite challenging and where I had to prepare well and the some introducing lectures which were easier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The relation between professors and students was a bit more formal but otherwise the style was pretty similar. We had both lectures and seminars. What I really liked was that there was always room and time for discussions in the seminars and generally discussion was a bigger part of the courses as what I've experienced at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Der Erwerb von Deutsch als Zweit- und Fremdsprache, Einführung in sprachwissenschaftliche Theorien, Genus und Geschlecht, Einführung in das Studium der Neueren deutschen Literatur, Postmigrantische Narrative and Medien, Film und Kultur. Film- und Medientheorien.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can highly recommend the courses Genus und Geschlecht (a linguistic course) and Postmigrantische Narrative (a literature course). The professors were really committed and we read a lot of very interesting texts and the themes were just very relevant and exciting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were a bit more expensive than I thought (close to Danish prices) but beer, chocolate and candy was very cheap and it was also less expensive to go out and eat as it is in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a broad selection of sport activities you could join and it was also pretty cheap. That was really cool. There was also a lot of social events for Erasmus-students like bike trips, parties and stuff like that.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I thought the sport activities were a great and easy way of meeting other student - also student who were not on exchange but lived there permanently.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city a lot, go for long walks and visit museums and the cultural institution. I also wished that I had traveled a bit more to other cities nearby so I would also recommend that.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was quite easy. The differences were not that many and I quickly adjusted.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The sport activities are a great opportunity of meeting local students and I would also recommend to live with Germans because that is probably the easiest way to get to know locals. Otherwise I can recommend the app 'Bumble' where you can get new friends and often local students who are new in the city use this app, so that is also a good way of getting in contact with locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Maybe the bureaucratic stuff - Germany can be a little old school on that matter, but it was not that big a problem.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people I met were all very open minded and friendly and were just inviting me to go a long ti different social activities and I really appreciated that. Then I also had the feeling that Germans are very spontaneous and would just ask "do want to go for a beer" or "should we go to the cinema tonight" instead of always planning ahead and I found that very refreshing and nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't stress to much about the paperwork, enjoy Sternschanze and all the other cool places in Hamborg and just try out different courses the first week of the semester and then choose the ones you found most interesting.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think the buddy program was a very good initiative and I recommend signing up for that.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I improved my verbal skills a lot and during my exchange I got a lot more comfortable talking German which was really nice. On a personal level it was also a very rewarding experience - you learn a lot about yourself when you move alone to a new city and a new country and I think you grow a lot from that.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: At times it was a bit lonely being on exchange but I think is almost inevitable not to feel lonely some of the time and I always found comfort in calling somebody from home or talking to my roommates, so it was not as bad as I had feared before going on exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I'm really happy that I went on exchange and I can only encourage all students to go!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
